The use of tranexamic acid (TXA) for the treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) is based on evidence derived from near-miss cases and criterion-based clinical audit concepts. This approach aims to address severe maternal complications, including PPH, effectively. 2. Collaboration with the WHO Reproductive Health and Research (RHR) and Maternal, Child, and Adolescent Health (MCA) departments is essential. Monitoring and evaluation teams will collect and assess data on the implementation of recommendations at both national and regional levels. This evaluation will occur in the shortto medium-term to determine the impact of the recommendations on national policies in individual WHO Member States. 3. The recommendation on the use of tranexamic acid for PPH treatment will be reviewed and prioritized annually by the Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG). This process will involve assessing the current portfolio of maternal and perinatal health recommendations and identifying new or existing questions for guideline development and updates. 4. If new evidence emerges that could potentially impact the current evidence base, the recommendation may be updated. In the absence of new reports or information, the recommendation may be revalidated. Following the publication and dissemination of updated recommendations, any concerns regarding their validity will be promptly communicated to guideline implementers, along with plans for further updates. 5. WHO encourages suggestions for additional questions to be included in the updated recommendations on tranexamic acid for PPH treatment. 6. The recommendation on tranexamic acid is supported by evidence from studies such as the WOMAN Trial (World Maternal Antifibrinolytic Trial), which demonstrated the efficacy of early administration of tranexamic acid in reducing mortality, hysterectomy rates, and other morbidities associated with PPH. This trial was an international, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. 7. The cost-effectiveness of administering tranexamic acid to bleeding trauma patients has been analyzed using data from the CRASH-2 trial, further supporting its use in acute severe hemorrhage scenarios. 8. The WHO guideline development process involves systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and the application of the GRADE methodology to assess the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations. This ensures that the recommendations are based on robust and transparent evidence. 9. The guideline development process includes input from external experts, WHO staff, and representatives from various regions and disciplines. Conflicts of interest are managed to ensure the integrity of the recommendations. 10. The updated recommendations consider critical outcomes such as maternal mortality (all causes and due to bleeding), delayed initiation of breastfeeding, prolonged hospitalization, and maternal temperature changes. These outcomes are evaluated to ensure the recommendations address the most significant clinical and public health concerns. 11. The WHO emphasizes the importance of equity, acceptability, and feasibility in implementing the recommendations. These factors are assessed to ensure that the guidelines are practical and beneficial across diverse healthcare settings, particularly in lowand middle-income countries. 12. The WHO guideline on tranexamic acid for PPH treatment is part of a broader effort to improve the quality of maternal and newborn care in health facilities, as outlined in the organization's standards for maternal and newborn health. 13. The guideline development process includes regular updates and reviews to incorporate new evidence and address emerging clinical and public health needs. This iterative process ensures that the recommendations remain relevant and effective in reducing maternal morbidity and mortality.
